items.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024
items.q: I’ve worn out my Freddie Hubbard book... those became like the same as the classical etudes that I would practice every day... really trying to mirror his phrasing

ctx.x: And sometimes I’ve read reviews and, in DownBeat, dissecting solos and trying to make sense of what someone’s doing over a certain chord symbol and the lengths that you may have to go to to say okay they’re playing the sharp nine here and they played it two bars before that. And I guess what I’m trying to say, sometimes it’s hard to explain why people do things. © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

Yeah, totally. And I think the most valuable thing is not — I mean it’s valuable to have an analysis of it for sure. But to me the most valuable thing is seeing — I mean I’ve worn out my Freddie Hubbard book that I think Hal Leonard might be the publisher of it. I mean those became like the same as the classical etudes that I would practice every day and like we called it they’re “Rochut Etudes” — these vocal etudes that are very, very standard in the trombone pedagogue world. But the Freddie Hubbard solos to me…
Do you feel driven to help in any way you can to keep the trombone alive?
